opts.zh: 後者——它也在同一時間漲價了

opts.en: Neither — both raised prices, so both are equally exposed
opts.zh: 都不是——兩家都漲價，代表兩家一樣容易受影響

opts.en: Can't tell without knowing gross margin
opts.zh: 不知道毛利率就無法判斷

opts.en: The first chain — it passed the pricing-power test
opts.zh: 前者——它通過了定價權測試

exp.en: A small volume drop after a real price increase is the direct pricing-power test this lesson describes — customers stayed even though it now costs more. A 15% volume drop shows customers are price-sensitive and will switch, which is the opposite signal. Both companies raising prices doesn't make them equally protected; what matters is what happened to volume afterward.
exp.zh: 漲價之後銷量只掉一點點，正是這一課講的定價權直接測試——即使變貴了，客戶還是留下來。銷量掉 15%代表消費者對價格敏感、會轉單，這是相反的訊號。兩家都漲價不代表兩家一樣有保障，重點是漲價之後銷量發生了什麼事。

q.en: A used-goods marketplace grows from 1 million to 10 million users, and both matching speed and closing price improve as it grows. A hardware retail chain grows from 50 to 500 stores, and per-store procurement cost falls due to bulk buying. Which advantage better fits the definition of a network effect?
q.zh: 一家二手交易平台使用者數從 100 萬成長到 1000 萬，媒合速度與成交價都跟著變好；一家五金連鎖賣場從 50 家店擴張到 500 家，因為採購量變大，單店採購成本下降。哪一個比較符合網路效應的定義？

opts.en: The marketplace — more users make the product better for existing users
opts.zh: 二手交易平台——用戶增加讓既有用戶得到更多價值

opts.en: The hardware chain — more scale lowered costs
opts.zh: 五金賣場——規模擴大降低了成本

opts.en: Both — they're the same mechanism at different scales
opts.zh: 兩者都是——只是規模不同，機制一樣

opts.en: Neither — user count and store count alone prove nothing
opts.zh: 都不是——單看用戶數或店數本身不能證明什麼

exp.en: Network effect means value, not just cost, rises with participants — the marketplace fits because matching speed and price genuinely improve as the user base grows. The hardware chain's improvement is a cost advantage from purchasing scale, a different mechanism entirely, even though both examples show a company getting bigger.
exp.zh: 網路效應指的是「價值」而不只是「成本」隨參與者增加而提升——二手平台符合這個定義，因為媒合速度和成交價確實隨用戶數變好。五金賣場的改善來自採購規模帶來的成本優勢，是完全不同的機制，即使兩個例子都是公司規模變大。

q.en: A cloud accounting platform's customers have used it for an average of 8 years; after a 15% price hike, renewal rate dropped just 1 point. A music streaming app raised prices 10% and lost 20% of subscribers within a month. Which one's switching cost is more likely real, not just habit?
q.zh: 一款雲端會計軟體的用戶平均用了 8 年；調漲訂閱費 15%後，續約率只掉了 1 個百分點。一款串流音樂 App 調漲 10%，一個月內流失了 20%的訂戶。哪一個的轉換成本比較可能是真的，而不只是慣性？

opts.en: The streaming app — its users had stuck around for years too
opts.zh: 串流 App——它的用戶也黏著很多年了

opts.en: Both — long tenure alone proves switching cost in either case
opts.zh: 兩者皆是——用了很久本身就代表轉換成本

opts.en: The accounting platform — it survived a real price-increase test
opts.zh: 會計軟體——它撐過了真正的漲價測試

opts.en: Neither — a single price increase isn't enough evidence
opts.zh: 都不是——一次漲價不足以當證據

exp.en: The accounting platform passed the only test that counts — churn barely moved after a larger price increase, consistent with real data-migration and retraining costs. The streaming app's users looked loyal right up until the test happened, then a 10% hike triggered a 20% loss — exactly the pattern of habit that was never priced, not a real switching cost.
exp.zh: 會計軟體通過了唯一算數的測試——即使漲幅更大，續訂率幾乎沒動，符合真實資料搬遷與重新訓練成本的樣子。串流 App 的用戶在被測試之前看起來也很忠誠，結果一次 10%的漲價就流失了 20%——這正是「從沒被漲價測試過的慣性」的典型樣子，不是真正的轉換成本。

q.en: Two phone brands both score above 90% in consumer brand-awareness surveys. One has raised average selling price steadily for five years while holding 35%+ gross margin; the other has cut average selling price for three straight years to defend shipment volume, with margin down to 18%. Which one more likely has a real intangible-asset moat, not just awareness?
q.zh: 兩個手機品牌在消費者調查裡的知名度都超過 90%。其中一家過去五年平均售價持續上升、毛利率穩定維持在 35%以上；另一家為了維持出貨量，過去三年平均售價持續下滑，毛利率跌到 18%。哪一家比較可能擁有真正的無形資產型護城河，而不只是知名度？

opts.en: The second — it's working harder to keep customers
opts.zh: 後者——它更努力留住客戶

opts.en: The first — pricing power sustained the margin
opts.zh: 前者——定價權讓毛利率撐住了

opts.en: Both equally — awareness is what matters, not price
opts.zh: 兩者一樣——重要的是知名度，不是價格

opts.en: Neither — margin depends on manufacturing cost, not brand
opts.zh: 都不是——毛利率是製造成本決定的，跟品牌無關

exp.en: Brand awareness is the same for both, which is exactly the point — awareness alone tells you nothing. The company that could keep raising prices while margin held is showing the actual evidence of an intangible-asset moat (pricing power); the one cutting price to defend volume is showing the opposite — its brand isn't buying it any pricing power at all.
exp.zh: 兩家的知名度一樣高，這正是重點——單看知名度什麼都看不出來。能持續漲價又守住毛利率的那家，才展現出無形資產護城河的真正證據（定價權）；靠降價維持出貨量的那家，展現的是相反的訊號——它的品牌根本沒有換來任何定價權。

q.en: A regional natural-gas distributor serves an area whose total demand can just barely cover one operator's fixed costs plus a reasonable profit. A second operator entering would push both into losses. Which moat source does this describe?
q.zh: 一家區域天然氣配送商，服務範圍的總需求量剛好只夠支撐一家業者打平固定成本並賺取合理利潤。如果第二家業者進場，雙方都會虧損。這最接近哪一種護城河來源？

opts.en: Cost advantage
opts.zh: 成本優勢

opts.en: Network effect
opts.zh: 網路效應

opts.en: Switching cost
opts.zh: 轉換成本

opts.en: Efficient scale
opts.zh: 有效規模

exp.en: This is the defining case of efficient scale: no patent, no brand, no habit — a rational second entrant simply does the arithmetic, sees the market can't profitably support two players, and stays out.
exp.zh: 這正是有效規模的定義案例：沒有專利、沒有品牌、沒有慣性——一個理性的第二家業者只是算過帳，發現這個市場撐不起兩家一起賺，於是選擇不進來。

q.en: In 2021, several ocean-shipping companies posted record profits and their stocks rallied together, driven by a global container shortage and freight-rate spike, not by any one company being harder to compete with. What does that profit surge mainly reflect?
q.zh: 2021 年，多家海運公司獲利創歷史新高、股價齊漲，原因是全球缺櫃與運價暴漲，不是哪一家公司特別難被取代。這波獲利成長主要反映的是什麼？

opts.en: Their moats got wider
opts.zh: 護城河變寬了

opts.en: An industry-wide cyclical tailwind
opts.zh: 產業順風（景氣循環）

opts.en: A jump in switching costs
opts.zh: 轉換成本提高了

opts.en: Better management across the industry
opts.zh: 整個產業的管理層突然變強了

exp.en: When every player's numbers move together for the same external, industry-wide reason, that's the tailwind test described earlier in this lesson — the industry got paid well, which is not the same as any single company having a durable edge over its rivals.
exp.zh: 當所有業者的數字，都因為同一個外部、產業層級的原因同時往同一個方向移動，這正是本課前面講的順風測試——是整個產業被市場多付了錢，跟某一家公司比對手更有優勢是不同的事。

q.en: A social platform was the first mover in its category and built an early lead in users and media buzz. Two years later, a later entrant with better features and a viral invite mechanism overtook it, and the original users largely migrated. What does this best illustrate?
q.zh: 一個社群平台是所屬類別最早上線的產品，累積了先發用戶與媒體聲量。兩年後，一個功能更好、有病毒式邀請機制的後進者迅速超車，原本的用戶大量轉移過去。這說明了什麼？

opts.en: Being first automatically becomes a network-effect moat over time
opts.zh: 先進場久了自然會變成網路效應護城河

opts.en: A first-mover lead only becomes a moat if it gets converted into a real source before a challenger arrives
opts.zh: 先行者的領先，只有在挑戰者出現之前被轉化成真正的來源，才會變成護城河

opts.en: This proves the category has no possible moat
opts.zh: 這證明這個類別根本不可能有護城河

opts.en: This proves network effects don't exist in social platforms
opts.zh: 這證明社群平台不存在網路效應

exp.en: Being first buys a head start, not a moat — the pitfall named earlier in this lesson. If that lead never gets converted into a real switching cost or a genuine network effect, a later entrant with a better product and a faster growth loop can and does take the users away, exactly as happened here.
exp.zh: 先進場買到的是起步優勢，不是護城河——這正是本課前面點名的陷阱。如果這個領先從沒被轉化成真正的轉換成本或真正的網路效應，一個產品更好、成長飛輪更快的後進者，完全可以、也確實會把用戶搶走，就像這個案例發生的一樣。

q.en: A home-goods retailer was recognized by nearly all shoppers in its country and had used the same well-known discount-coupon promotion for decades. Same-store sales and margins eroded for years, and the chain filed for bankruptcy with roughly 84% fewer stores than its peak. What does this best show?
q.zh: 一家家居用品連鎖店，幾乎所有消費者都認得它，而且用了同一套知名折價券促銷手法長達數十年。同店銷售與毛利率卻連續多年下滑，公司最後聲請破產，門市數比高峰時期少了大約 84%。這最能說明什麼？

opts.en: High brand awareness on its own is not switching cost or pricing power
opts.zh: 單靠高知名度，不等於轉換成本或定價權

opts.en: The coupon promotion proves the company had real pricing power
opts.zh: 優惠券促銷證明公司擁有真正的定價權

opts.en: 84% fewer stores means the company must have had a network effect that broke
opts.zh: 門市少了八成四，代表公司一定曾經有網路效應、後來破功

opts.en: Bankruptcy always means a company never had any moat source
opts.zh: 破產就代表公司從來沒有任何一種護城河來源

exp.en: Widespread recognition and a long-running promotion produced awareness, not a moat — the coupon habit actually trained customers to buy only at a discount, which is closer to eroding pricing power than building it. This is the 'recognition without preference' look-alike this lesson names for intangible assets: knowing the name is not the same as being willing to pay more for it.
exp.zh: 廣泛的知名度加上一套用了很久的促銷手法，製造出來的是「知名度」，不是護城河——那張優惠券其實訓練了客戶只在打折時才買，這比較接近侵蝕定價權，不是建立定價權。這正是本課在無形資產那一節點名的「有知名度、沒有偏好」假象：叫得出名字，不等於願意為它多付錢。

q.en: You are testing a company for a moat by comparing its gross margin with its closest peer's. The only three years of data you have are the three years of a severe industry-wide shortage, when both companies posted record margins. What is the main problem with that comparison?
q.zh: 你想用「和最接近的同業比毛利率」來檢驗一家公司有沒有護城河，但手上只拿得到 3 年資料，而這 3 年剛好都是全產業嚴重缺貨、兩家公司毛利率都創新高的年份。這樣比較的主要問題是什麼？

opts.en: No problem — a boom is exactly when the stronger company pulls furthest ahead of the weaker one
opts.zh: 沒有問題——景氣大好的時候，正是強者把弱者甩得最開的時候

opts.en: A shortage lifts the weaker producer the most, so the peer gap is at its narrowest precisely then — the comparison will understate the difference between them
opts.zh: 缺貨對體質較弱的那一家拉抬最多，所以同業落差恰好在那時候最窄——這樣比會低估兩家之間真正的差距

opts.en: Gross margin can never be compared between two companies
opts.zh: 毛利率本來就不能拿兩家公司互相比較

opts.en: Three years is always enough as long as the two companies are a similar size
opts.zh: 只要兩家公司規模相近，3 年資料就一定夠用

exp.en: When everything is sold out, even ordinary capacity gets priced as if it were scarce, so the weakest capable producer gains the most margin — the gap you are trying to measure gets compressed exactly at the top. The first option is the common intuition and it is backwards. The fix is not more years of the same kind: find one bad year and measure the gap there.
exp.zh: 當所有產能都賣光時，連普通的產能都會被當成稀缺品定價，所以體質最弱、但還能量產的那一家毛利率拉升最多——你想量的那道落差，恰好在最高點被壓扁。第一個選項是多數人的直覺，而且方向正好相反。解法不是再多找幾個同類型的好年份，而是找出一個壞年冬，在那一年量落差。

q.en: Company X's ROIC over five years: 8%, 31%, 6%, 29%, 9%. Company Y's over the same five years: 19%, 20%, 18%, 21%, 19%. Which is more likely to have a real moat, even though their averages are fairly close?
q.zh: X 公司 5 年 ROIC 依序為 8%、31%、6%、29%、9%；Y 公司同期依序為 19%、20%、18%、21%、19%。即使兩家的平均值算出來相近，哪一家比較可能有真正的護城河？

opts.en: Company X, because its best year is much higher
opts.zh: X 公司，因為它最高的那一年數字更高

opts.en: Both are equally good, since the averages are close
opts.zh: 兩家一樣好，因為平均值很接近

opts.en: Neither — five years is not enough data to say anything
opts.zh: 兩家都無法判斷——5 年的資料不夠多

opts.en: Company Y, because its level is stable across all five years
opts.zh: Y 公司，因為它 5 年下來水準都很穩定

exp.en: X's wild swing (6% to 31%) points to something outside its control setting the return — likely a commodity or cyclical factor. Y's tight band around ~19-21% is the signature of a defended, repeatable edge.
exp.zh: X 公司的大幅擺盪（6% 到 31%）指向報酬率是被某個公司控制不了的因素決定的——很可能是原物料或景氣循環因素。Y 公司緊貼在約 19% 到 21% 之間的窄幅波動，才是有人守住、可重複優勢的特徵。

q.en: Industry-wide input costs rise 10% this year. Company X's gross margin falls from 42% to 41%; Company Y's falls from 35% to 27%. What does this most likely indicate?
q.zh: 今年產業原物料成本普遍上漲了 10%。X 公司毛利率從 42% 微降到 41%；Y 公司毛利率從 35% 大跌到 27%。這最可能代表什麼？

opts.en: X likely has stronger pricing power than Y, passing the cost through with little margin damage
opts.zh: X 的定價權可能比 Y 強，幾乎把成本轉嫁出去，毛利幾乎沒受傷

opts.en: Y's products are simply worse quality
opts.zh: Y 的產品品質比較差

opts.en: A falling margin means Y is growing faster
opts.zh: 毛利率下滑代表 Y 成長得比較快

opts.en: Neither company has a moat because both margins fell somewhat
opts.zh: 兩家公司都沒有護城河，因為毛利率都有下滑

exp.en: A 1-point margin loss versus an 8-point loss under the same cost shock is exactly the pricing power test: X passed most of the cost through, Y absorbed most of it.
exp.zh: 同樣的成本衝擊下，一個只掉 1 個百分點、一個掉了 8 個百分點，這正是定價權測試要看的東西：X 把大部分成本轉嫁出去了，Y 則大部分自己吸收下來。

q.en: What does the "pricing power test" specifically check?
q.zh: 「定價權測試」具體在測什麼？

opts.en: Whether the company can raise price to offset a cost increase without a proportional drop in volume
opts.zh: 公司能不能靠漲價抵銷成本上漲，同時銷量不會等比例下滑

opts.en: Whether the company's stock price has gone up recently
opts.zh: 公司的股價最近有沒有上漲

opts.en: Whether the company's gross margin is above 50%
opts.zh: 公司的毛利率是否超過 50%

opts.en: Whether the company has publicly announced a price increase
opts.zh: 公司有沒有公開宣布調漲售價

exp.en: An announced price increase (the last option) is not evidence on its own — plenty of announced increases get walked back or fail to hold once volume drops. The test is the outcome: margin and volume together after the increase actually takes effect.
exp.zh: 公開宣布調漲（最後一個選項）本身不算證據——很多宣布的漲價後來會撤回，或漲價後銷量掉太多而撐不住。真正的測試看的是結果：漲價真正生效之後，毛利率和銷量同時發生了什麼事。

q.en: Company B's share rises from 18% to 26% over three years, while its average selling price falls 15% and gross margin falls from 30% to 17%. What is really happening?
q.zh: B 公司的市佔率從 18% 漲到 26%，但同期平均售價下跌了 15%、毛利率從 30% 掉到 17%。這比較像哪一種情況？

opts.en: The moat is widening because customers are switching to a better product
opts.zh: 護城河正在變寬，客戶被更好的產品吸引

opts.en: This is a clear strategic mistake that should be abandoned immediately
opts.zh: 這是明顯的策略錯誤，應該立刻放棄

opts.en: The company is buying share with discounts, not earning it with a moat
opts.zh: 公司在用降價買市佔率，不是靠護城河贏來的

opts.en: There is not enough information to say anything
opts.zh: 資料不足以判斷任何事

exp.en: Share up while price and margin fall together is the textbook signature of buying share — sustainable only as long as the discounting continues, and reversible the moment it stops.
exp.zh: 份額上升，同時價格和毛利率一起下滑，是花錢買份額的教科書特徵——只要還在補貼折扣就能延續，一旦停止就會反轉。

q.en: The three biggest players in a niche all report ROIC above 35% this year, versus about 18% the year before, all moving together. What does this most likely mean?
q.zh: 某細分產業的三大龍頭同一年 ROIC 都衝上 35% 以上，前一年平均只有約 18%，三家幾乎同步。這最可能代表什麼？

opts.en: All three companies independently widened their moat this year
opts.zh: 這三家公司今年都各自把護城河變寬了

opts.en: One of the three must have misreported its numbers
opts.zh: 這三家裡一定有一家數字有誤

opts.en: A high ROIC this year guarantees the stock will keep rising
opts.zh: 今年 ROIC 高，代表股價一定會繼續漲

opts.en: The industry is likely riding a temporary cycle or tailwind, not evidence of any single firm's durable edge
opts.zh: 產業很可能正搭上一個暫時的循環或順風，不代表任何一家公司有持續的個別優勢

exp.en: A moat is a firm-specific edge over rivals — when the closest rivals move together, the shared movement points at something common to the industry, not at any one company's protected position.
exp.zh: 護城河是一家公司相對於對手的個別優勢——當最接近的對手同步一起變動時，這個「同步」指向的是產業共同的東西，不是任何一家公司被保護住的位置。

q.en: A company earns a steady 28% ROIC but has made almost no new capex or acquisitions for three years, returning nearly all free cash flow via buybacks. What is this closest to?
q.zh: 一家公司 ROIC 常年維持 28%，但過去 3 年幾乎沒有新增資本支出或併購，多出來的現金幾乎全部拿去回購股票。這比較接近哪一種情況？

opts.en: A cash cow — a real, defended return with limited room to redeploy new capital at the same rate, not evidence of no moat
opts.zh: 一台現金牛——真實、守得住的高報酬，但沒什麼地方可以用同樣報酬率再投入新資本，不代表沒有護城河

opts.en: Wasteful management destroying shareholder value
opts.zh: 管理層在浪費現金，正在破壞股東價值

opts.en: A widening moat, because buybacks boost per-share metrics
opts.zh: 護城河正在變寬，因為回購推高了每股數字

opts.en: Not enough information to say anything
opts.zh: 資料不足，無法判斷

exp.en: High stable ROIC proves the moat; it says nothing about whether new capital can be redeployed at that same rate. No reinvestment options plus high ROIC is a cash-return business, a legitimate but different kind of holding from a compounder.
exp.zh: 高而穩定的 ROIC 證明了護城河存在；但沒說明新資本還能不能用同樣報酬率再投入。沒有再投資機會加上高 ROIC，就是一台現金回饋型的生意，是合理但和複利機不同種類的持股。

q.en: A company trades at 45x forward earnings versus a peer median of 22x, and management explains it away as "our technology is unique." What should you do before accepting that premium as justified?
q.zh: 一家公司本益比是 45 倍，同業中位數是 22 倍，管理層解釋是「因為我們技術比較獨特」。在接受這個溢價合理之前，應該先做什麼？

opts.en: Accept management's explanation since they know the business best
opts.zh: 直接接受管理層的說法，因為他們最懂自己的公司

opts.en: Go back and check whether ROIC, pricing power, and share/price evidence actually support a premium that size
opts.zh: 回頭檢查 ROIC、定價權、份額與價格的證據是不是真的撐得起這麼大的溢價

opts.en: Assume any premium above peers is automatically a bubble and avoid the stock
opts.zh: 直接假設任何高於同業的溢價就是泡沫，應該迴避

opts.en: Check whether the stock price has risen over the past six months
opts.zh: 看股價過去半年有沒有上漲來判斷

exp.en: A large premium needs a checkable reason, not an adjective. The evidence gathered in this lesson is exactly what should be used to stress-test whether the premium is earned or simply optimism priced in.
exp.zh: 大溢價需要一個可以檢驗的理由，不是一個形容詞。這一課蒐集的證據，正是用來壓力測試這個溢價是不是真的賺來的、還是只是市場把樂觀情緒定價進去。

q.en: Company M has held roughly 30% ROIC for nine straight years. Company N just jumped to 30% this year, up from 9% two years ago, during an industry-wide shortage. Which one needs more scrutiny before you assume the same durability, and why?
q.zh: M 公司過去 9 年 ROIC 一直穩定在約 30%。N 公司今年 ROIC 才剛跳到 30%，2 年前還只有 9%，跳升發生在一波全產業性的缺料期間。在假設兩者持續期一樣之前，哪一家需要更多檢視？為什麼？

opts.en: M, because a long steady run is always the first to mean-revert
opts.zh: M，因為穩定維持最久的公司通常最先均值回歸

opts.en: N, because a ROIC that moves that fast in two years must be an accounting error
opts.zh: N，因為 ROIC 兩年內跳這麼快一定是會計問題

opts.en: N, because a shortage-driven spike is a classic false signal for durability
opts.zh: N，因為缺料帶來的暴衝是持續期最常見的假訊號

opts.en: Neither — 30% clears any reasonable durability bar regardless of how it got there
opts.zh: 兩家都不用，30% 不管怎麼來的都已經過關

exp.en: A ROIC spike coinciding with an industry-wide shortage is exactly the false signal this lesson opens with — it usually reflects temporary pricing power from scarcity, not a durable structural edge, and tends to fade once supply catches up. M's steady nine-year run is actually the more reassuring pattern, not the riskier one. The option blaming an accounting error mistakes a real, if temporary, economic cause for fraud.
exp.zh: ROIC 暴衝剛好碰上全產業缺料，正是這一課一開始點出的典型假訊號——它通常反映的是稀缺帶來的暫時性訂價權，不是持續的結構優勢，一旦供給跟上通常就會消退。M 維持 9 年的穩定表現，其實是比較讓人放心的型態，不是比較危險的型態。把它歸咎於會計問題的那個選項，是把一個真實（雖然是暫時的）經濟原因誤判成做假帳。

q.en: A specialty distributor reports a 2% net margin but turns its invested capital 12 times a year, giving a ROIC around 24%. It also collects cash in 25 days but pays its own suppliers in 60 days. Before dismissing this as a low-quality business, what should you check?
q.zh: 一家專業經銷商淨利率只有 2%，但一年把投入資本周轉 12 次，算出來的 ROIC 大約 24%。它收現只要 25 天，付供應商貨款卻要 60 天。在把它判定成一門平庸的生意之前，應該先檢查什麼？

opts.en: The cash conversion cycle — a negative one means the business is effectively running on its suppliers' capital, not weak-margin luck
opts.zh: 現金轉換循環——如果是負的，代表這門生意其實是用供應商的資本在運作，不是靠僥倖撐出薄利多銷

opts.en: Nothing — a 2% margin is disqualifying regardless of turnover
opts.zh: 不用檢查什麼，淨利率只有 2% 不管週轉率多少都直接淘汰

opts.en: Whether the turnover ratio was miscalculated, since distributors cannot realistically turn capital 12 times a year
opts.zh: 先查週轉率是不是算錯了，因為經銷商不可能一年周轉資本 12 次

opts.en: Whether the reported ROIC is fraudulent, since margin and turnover this different from each other cannot both be real
opts.zh: 先查申報的 ROIC 是不是造假，因為利益率和週轉率差這麼多不可能同時是真的

exp.en: Paying suppliers in 60 days while collecting cash in 25 means the company is essentially float-financed — it is holding onto other people's money for 35 days a cycle, which is a genuine, checkable source of capital efficiency, not an accounting artifact. This is exactly the low-margin, high-turnover quadrant this lesson describes as the most commonly misjudged. High turnover for a distributor is completely normal — inventory and receivables move fast relative to a comparatively small capital base.
exp.zh: 付供應商貨款要 60 天、收現卻只要 25 天，代表這家公司本質上是靠浮存資金在運作——它每個循環多握著別人的錢 35 天，這是真實、可查證的資本效率來源，不是做帳花招。這正是這一課描述最常被誤判的低利益率、高週轉象限。經銷商週轉快是完全正常的現象，存貨和應收帳款相對於偏小的資本基礎，本來就轉得快。

q.en: A skincare brand reports a 70% repeat-purchase rate and calls it a loyalty moat. A new competitor launches an almost identical formula at a lower price and reaches a similar repeat rate within four months. What does this most likely indicate?
q.zh: 一家保養品牌公布 70% 的回購率，並稱這是忠誠度護城河。一個新競爭者推出幾乎一樣的配方、價格更低，在 4 個月內也做到差不多的回購率。這最可能說明什麼？

opts.en: The original brand's moat is intact, since it still keeps its own 70% of customers
opts.zh: 原品牌的護城河沒事，因為它自己那 70% 的客戶還在

opts.en: Repeat-purchase rate is not a valid proxy for anything and should never be used
opts.zh: 回購率根本不是有效的代理指標，永遠不該拿來用

opts.en: The new entrant must be selling at a loss, since matching an incumbent's repeat rate this fast is otherwise impossible
opts.zh: 新進者一定是在賠錢賣，否則不可能這麼快追上原品牌的回購率

opts.en: The 70% repeat rate was measuring habit or satisfaction, not real switching cost — the true decision-level test failed
opts.zh: 70% 的回購率量到的其實是習慣或滿意度，不是真正的轉換成本——真正在決策層級的測試沒有通過

exp.en: A repeat-purchase rate measured only against a brand's own existing base tells you customers who already buy keep buying — it does not test whether they would resist an easy, cheaper, near-identical alternative. The moment a close substitute reaches a similar repeat rate almost immediately, it reveals that customers were never actually locked in; they were just satisfied enough not to have looked elsewhere yet. That is a demand-base or habit signal, not the decision-level substitutability test this lesson asks for.
exp.zh: 只用品牌自己現有的客戶群去算的回購率，只能告訴你已經在買的人會繼續買——並不能測試他們面對一個容易取得、更便宜、幾乎一樣的替代品時會不會抵抗。當一個相近替代品幾乎立刻就做到相近的回購率，就代表客戶其實從來沒有被真正鎖住；他們只是滿意到還沒動念去找別的選擇。這是需求基礎或習慣訊號，不是這一課要求的決策層級可替代性測試。

q.en: During a recession, Product A's revenue at a company kept growing, while Product B from the same company saw cancellations spike — even though both had shown similarly high renewal rates the year before. What is the most likely explanation?
q.zh: 景氣衰退期間，同一家公司的 A 產品營收持續成長，B 產品卻出現退訂潮暴增——即使前一年兩者的續約率看起來一樣高。最可能的解釋是什麼？

opts.en: B's renewal rate data must have been reported incorrectly the prior year
opts.zh: B 前一年公布的續約率資料一定有誤

opts.en: A and B sit at different points on the want-versus-need spectrum, and the prior year's renewal rate did not reveal that difference because it had not yet been tested by a real budget squeeze
opts.zh: A 和 B 在想要與需要的光譜上位置不同，而前一年的續約率沒有揭露這個差異，因為當時還沒真正被預算緊縮的情境考驗過

opts.en: Recessions always hit newer products harder than older ones, regardless of what they do
opts.zh: 不管產品性質為何，衰退期一定是較新的產品受傷比較重

opts.en: A is simply a better product than B
opts.zh: 純粹是 A 的產品做得比 B 好

exp.en: A stable renewal rate measured in a normal environment does not test what happens when a customer's budget is actually under pressure — that is precisely the 'what happens if this purchase is delayed a year' test this lesson uses for the demand-base checkpoint. The recession is the real test; the prior year's renewal number was measuring something else, either routine or a budget that had not yet been squeezed.
exp.zh: 在正常環境下量到的穩定續約率，並沒有測試到客戶預算真正吃緊時會發生什麼事——這正是這一課用在需求基礎檢查點的「如果延後一年購買會怎樣」測試。衰退才是真正的考驗；前一年的續約數字量到的其實是別的東西，不是例行公事，就是還沒被壓縮到的預算。

q.en: Which of the following best illustrates the 'social tolerance' checkpoint, using the pattern this lesson describes with card-payment interchange fees?
q.zh: 以下哪一項最能說明「社會容忍度」這道檢查點，套用這一課描述的刷卡手續費歷史模式？

opts.en: A single regulator capped the fee once, and every other market immediately followed the same rule
opts.zh: 只有一個監管機構設限過一次，其他市場就立刻跟進採用同一套規則

opts.en: The fee has never actually been capped anywhere, only threatened
opts.zh: 手續費其實從來沒有真的被設限過，只有被威脅過

opts.en: Several separate governments, years apart, each independently capped a legally earned fee once it came to be seen as a hidden tax on an everyday necessity
opts.zh: 好幾個不同國家的政府，在相隔多年的不同時間點，各自獨立對一項合法賺取的費用設下上限——因為它開始被看成是強加在日常必需品上的隱形稅

opts.en: The fee was capped because the company's ROIC was mathematically too high by an objective formula
opts.zh: 手續費被設限，是因為有一個客觀公式判定公司的 ROIC 數學上太高

exp.en: The interchange-fee history spans multiple independent jurisdictions and years, each acting on its own political read of the same pattern, a legally earned but arguably hidden fee sitting on top of a near-universal daily transaction, not from a shared formula or a single ruling that cascaded elsewhere. That independence across jurisdictions and time is exactly why this checkpoint is treated as a real, recurring risk rather than a one-off event.
exp.zh: 刷卡手續費被設限的歷史橫跨好幾個各自獨立的司法管轄區與年份——每一個都是根據自己對同一種型態（一項合法賺取、卻可以說是隱藏在近乎人人每天都會用到的交易上的費用）的政治判斷行動，不是套用同一個公式或由單一裁定擴散出去。橫跨不同司法管轄區與時間點各自獨立發生，正是這個檢查點被當成真實、會反覆發生的風險，而不是一次性事件的原因。

q.en: Company Z's NOPAT rose from $50M to $53M after it reinvested $20M the prior year. Its trailing five-year average ROIC is 22%. What is its incremental ROIC, and what does that suggest about using the 22% average to model next year's growth?
q.zh: Z 公司在前一年再投資 2,000 萬美元之後，NOPAT 從 5,000 萬美元成長到 5,300 萬美元。它過去 5 年的平均 ROIC 是 22%。它的增量 ROIC 是多少？這對用 22% 平均值去建模明年成長，說明了什麼？

opts.en: Incremental ROIC is 22%, matching the average exactly, so the average is safe to use
opts.zh: 增量 ROIC 剛好等於 22% 的平均值，所以用平均值是安全的

opts.en: Incremental ROIC cannot be calculated from this information
opts.zh: 光憑這些資訊算不出增量 ROIC

opts.en: Incremental ROIC is 265%, since $53M divided by $20M is the correct formula
opts.zh: 增量 ROIC 是 265%，因為 5,300 萬除以 2,000 萬才是正確算法

opts.en: Incremental ROIC is 15% — well below the 22% average, so using the average would overstate the growth ceiling
opts.zh: 增量 ROIC 是 15%——明顯低於 22% 的平均值，所以用平均值會高估成長天花板

exp.en: Incremental ROIC is delta NOPAT over the prior period's net reinvestment: ($53M minus $50M) divided by $20M equals 15%. That is meaningfully below the 22% historical average, meaning the newest capital deployed is earning less than the historical average — exactly the pitfall this lesson warns about. The 265% option uses the wrong denominator — this period's NOPAT instead of the prior period's net reinvestment.
exp.zh: 增量 ROIC ＝ ΔNOPAT 除以前一期的淨再投資：（5,300 萬－5,000 萬）÷ 2,000 萬＝15%。這明顯低於 22% 的歷史平均，代表最新投入的資本賺到的報酬，比歷史平均還差——這正是這一課提醒的陷阱。算成 265% 的那個選項用錯了分母（用了本期 NOPAT，而不是前一期的淨再投資金額）。

q.en: Company W returns 90% of its free cash flow through buybacks, reports a reinvestment rate of just 5%, and describes itself as a '23% ROIC business.' What does that combination most likely mean for its growth ceiling?
q.zh: W 公司把 90% 的自由現金流拿去回購股票，公布的再投資率只有 5%，並自稱是「23% ROIC 的優質企業」。這個組合對它的成長天花板最可能代表什麼？

opts.en: Buybacks add directly to invested capital, so they should be counted as reinvestment in this formula
opts.zh: 回購會直接加進投入資本，所以在這個公式裡應該算成再投資

opts.en: The endogenous growth ceiling is very low, roughly 23% times 5% is about 1%, regardless of how high the ROIC figure is
opts.zh: 內生成長天花板非常低——大約 23%×5%≈1%——不管 ROIC 數字看起來多高都一樣

opts.en: The growth ceiling must be close to 23%, since that is the reported ROIC
opts.zh: 成長天花板一定接近 23%，因為那是公布的 ROIC

opts.en: A 90% buyback ratio always signals a company in financial distress
opts.zh: 回購比率高達 90% 一定代表公司財務出狀況

exp.en: The growth ceiling formula multiplies incremental ROIC by the reinvestment rate, not the historical ROIC in isolation — a high ROIC on a tiny reinvestment rate still produces a tiny growth ceiling. Buybacks return cash to shareholders and fund EPS growth through a shrinking share count, but add nothing to invested capital, so they contribute nothing to the incremental-ROIC side of this formula — exactly the pitfall this lesson names.
exp.zh: 成長天花板公式是增量 ROIC 乘以再投資率，不是單獨看歷史 ROIC。再投資率小到只有 5%，就算 ROIC 再高，算出來的成長天花板還是很小。回購把現金還給股東，靠縮減股數撐 EPS 成長，但完全不會加進投入資本，因此對這個公式的增量 ROIC 那一側毫無貢獻——這正是這一課點名的陷阱。

q.en: Company R's trailing five-year average ROIC is 21% and has barely moved. Over those same five years its annual capital expenditure roughly doubled while operating profit was flat, and its largest new plant has not yet shipped a product. Which reading of that stable average is right?
q.zh: R 公司過去 5 年的平均 ROIC 是 21%，幾乎沒有變動。但在同樣這 5 年裡，它的年度資本支出大約翻了一倍，營業利益卻持平，而它最大的一座新廠到現在還沒出過貨。對這個「穩定的平均值」，哪一種解讀才對？

opts.en: High but falling — the average stays flattering for years because older assets sit in the denominator at written-down values while the newest, largest capital has produced nothing yet
opts.zh: 高但降——平均值之所以還漂亮好幾年，是因為舊資產以折舊後的帳面值躺在分母裡，而最新、金額最大的那筆資本還什麼都沒生出來

opts.en: High and flat — a five-year average that has not moved is itself the evidence that the return is durable
opts.zh: 高且穩——5 年平均值沒有變動，本身就是報酬持續的證據

opts.en: Low but rising — heavy capital expenditure is a reliable sign that returns are about to improve
opts.zh: 低但升——大額資本支出是報酬即將改善的可靠訊號

opts.en: The quadrant cannot be judged at all without first splitting the ROIC into margin and turnover
opts.zh: 不先把 ROIC 拆成利益率和週轉率，根本無法判斷象限

exp.en: Capital expenditure rising while operating profit is flat is the specific combination that identifies the high-but-falling box, and it shows up in the cash flow statement years before it shows up in an average ROIC. The tempting wrong answer is the second one: a stable average is a weighted memory of every investment ever made, so it keeps reading well precisely while the newest capital is earning nothing — stability of the average is not evidence of durability. The margin-turnover split explains how the company reached 21%, which is a useful but different question; what settles this one is the incremental ROIC on the capital just deployed.
exp.zh: 資本支出往上跑、營業利益卻持平，正是用來辨認「高但降」這一格的特定組合，而且它出現在現金流量表上的時間，比反映到平均 ROIC 上早好幾年。最誘人的錯誤答案是第二個：平均值是一份把歷來每一筆投資都加權進去的記憶，所以最新資本什麼都沒賺到的那段期間，它反而還是好看的——平均值穩定，不等於持續期的證據。把 ROIC 拆成利益率和週轉率，解釋的是這家公司「怎麼走到 21%」，那是有用但不同的問題；真正能定案的，是剛投下去那筆資本的增量 ROIC。

q.en: A company has an A- moat rating that has been slowly narrowing for two years. A competitor has a B moat rating that has been steadily widening for the same two years. For a five-year holding decision, which piece of information matters most?
q.zh: 一家公司護城河等級是 A-，但過去兩年一直在緩慢變窄；它的對手等級是 B，但同一段時間一直在穩定變寬。對一個 5 年的持有決定來說，哪個資訊最重要？

opts.en: The A- rating, because a higher starting grade always wins over a five-year horizon
opts.zh: A-這個等級，因為起始等級比較高，5 年下來一定會贏

opts.en: The direction of each trend, because it says more about where each company will be in five years than today's letter grade does
opts.zh: 兩者各自的趨勢方向，因為它比今天的字母等級更能說明 5 年後兩家公司會在哪裡

opts.en: Neither — only the current stock price of each company matters
opts.zh: 都不重要——只有目前的股價才重要

exp.en: This is the lesson's central point: a rating is a snapshot, a trend is a velocity, and a five-year decision is a bet on where each curve is headed, not on where it stands today. A narrowing A- and a widening B can cross well within five years.
exp.zh: 這正是本課的核心重點：等級是快照，趨勢是速度，而一個 5 年的決定，賭的是每條曲線接下來要往哪裡走，不是它今天站在哪裡。一個正在變窄的 A-和一個正在變寬的 B，完全可能在 5 年之內就交叉。

q.en: An analyst report lists five reasons a company's moat is intact and includes no discussion at all of any competitive threat. What does this most likely reveal?
q.zh: 一份分析報告列出五個護城河完好的理由，完全沒有討論任何競爭威脅。這最可能透露什麼？

opts.en: The moat is genuinely very strong, since five reasons were found
opts.zh: 護城河真的很強，因為找到了五個理由

opts.en: The report is simply too short and needs more detail on each of the five reasons
opts.zh: 這份報告只是寫得不夠詳細，五個理由都需要再補充細節

opts.en: Only one search track ran — the report has not yet done the work of hunting for narrowing evidence
opts.zh: 只跑了一條搜尋軸線——這份報告還沒做過主動尋找變窄證據的工作

exp.en: The number of supporting reasons says nothing about whether the opposing search was ever attempted. A report with zero discussion of competitive threats is the structural tell of a one-track search, regardless of how well-argued the five bullish reasons are.
exp.zh: 支持理由的數量，完全說明不了相反方向的搜尋有沒有被嘗試過。一份對競爭威脅完全沒有討論的報告，不管那五個看多理由寫得多有說服力，本身就是只跑了一條搜尋軸線的結構性破綻。

q.en: A memory-chip maker reports a weak quarter as the industry works through oversupply, right around the same time a major competitor exits the business entirely due to a debt collapse. What is the most defensible reading?
q.zh: 一家記憶體晶片廠公布了一個因為產業正在消化供過於求而疲弱的季度，差不多同一時間，一家主要對手因為債務問題整個退出了這門生意。最站得住腳的解讀是什麼？

opts.en: The weak quarter proves the whole industry's moat is narrowing
opts.zh: 這個疲弱的季度證明整個產業的護城河都在變窄

opts.en: Nothing can be concluded until next quarter's earnings are reported
opts.zh: 什麼都無法判斷，要等下一季財報公布才知道

opts.en: The competitor's exit is itself a leading indicator of tighter future supply discipline, even though it arrives dressed as bad news in the same quarter
opts.zh: 對手退出本身就是未來供給紀律收緊的先行指標，即使它是以同一季的壞消息形式出現

exp.en: This is the counter-intuitive case this lesson names explicitly: a competitor exit is bad-news-shaped in the quarter it happens, but it is structurally a widening signal for the survivors, delivered years before the pricing benefit shows up in anyone's margin. Reading the weak quarter as automatically bearish for the whole industry misses this.
exp.zh: 這正是本課明確點名的反直覺情況：對手退出在發生的那一季看起來像壞消息，但對留下來的廠商來說，這在結構上是一個變寬的訊號，而且會比定價效益反映在任何人的毛利率上，早了好幾年出現。把疲弱的一季直接當成整個產業的利空，會漏掉這一點。

q.en: A company's stock has fallen 35% over six months, in line with a broad sell-off across its entire sector, while none of the seven leading indicators covered in this lesson show any change. What should this most likely be read as?
q.zh: 一家公司的股價 6 個月內跌了 35%，跌幅跟整個類股的全面拋售一致，而本課提到的七個先行指標一個都沒有變化。這最應該被解讀成什麼？

opts.en: Strong evidence the moat is narrowing, since the stock has clearly fallen
opts.zh: 護城河正在變窄的強力證據，因為股價明顯下跌了

opts.en: A price move that likely has little to do with the moat trend itself, since none of the fundamental indicators changed
opts.zh: 一個很可能跟護城河趨勢本身沒什麼關係的價格波動，因為基本面指標一個都沒變

opts.en: Impossible to interpret without more data
opts.zh: 沒有更多資料就無法解讀

exp.en: Moat trend and stock-price trend are different measurements. A sector-wide sell-off with no change in customer concentration, insourcing, the price-share quadrant, margin slope, competitor capacity, technology position, or regulation is exactly the case this lesson warns about — price action carrying no information about the underlying trend.
exp.zh: 護城河趨勢和股價趨勢是兩個不同的量測。一次全類股的拋售，卻沒有任何客戶集中度、自研動向、價格份額象限、毛利率斜率、對手產能、技術地位、監管上的變化，正是本課特別提醒的情況——價格波動本身沒有透露底層趨勢的任何資訊。

q.en: Two holdings sit side by side. In company X the moat rates excellent today, but two of the leading indicators have deteriorated over the past two years. In company Y the moat rates mediocre, and two of the indicators have improved. Which one is more likely to end up monitored too loosely?
q.zh: 手上有兩檔並排的持股。X 公司的護城河現在評下來是優秀的，但過去兩年有兩個先行指標在惡化；Y 公司的護城河只評到中等，但有兩個先行指標在改善。哪一檔比較可能最後被盯得太鬆？

opts.en: X — the excellent current rating creates a false sense that nothing needs watching, so the deterioration is the one most likely to run unchecked
opts.zh: X——現在這個優秀的等級會製造一種不用再盯的錯覺，所以惡化反而最可能一路沒被攔下來

opts.en: Y — a mediocre moat always demands more attention than an excellent one, whatever the direction
opts.zh: Y——中等的護城河永遠比優秀的需要更多關注，跟方向無關

opts.en: Neither — monitoring effort should be identical across every holding regardless of what the indicators show
opts.zh: 都不會——不管指標怎麼走，每一檔持股投入的追蹤心力都該一樣

exp.en: The excellent-and-narrowing shape is the dangerous one precisely because the snapshot keeps looking fine while the trajectory has already turned — that is what happened to Blockbuster and to Intel for most of a decade. Y is the opposite: a mediocre rating already keeps attention on the position, and improving indicators are the cheap kind of surprise. Equal monitoring across every holding sounds disciplined but ignores the information in the indicators, which is exactly what the indicators are for.
exp.zh: 「等級優秀、方向往下」之所以是最危險的組合，正是因為快照一直看起來沒事，走勢卻早就轉向了——百視達是這樣，英特爾也這樣走了將近 10 年。Y 則正好相反：中等的等級本身就會讓人保持注意，而指標在改善是那種便宜的意外。至於「每一檔都盯得一樣緊」聽起來很有紀律，實際上是把指標透露的資訊丟掉了，而指標存在的目的就是要拿來分配注意力。

q.en: A two-year-old company with no established customer base yet shows rapid revenue growth but no clear evidence of any of the five moat sources. Is the moat-trend framework from this lesson the right tool to apply here?
q.zh: 一家成立兩年、還沒有穩定客戶基礎的公司，營收快速成長，但完全看不出五種護城河來源裡的任何一種。這一課的護城河趨勢框架，是適用於這裡的工具嗎？

opts.en: Yes — every company has a moat trend from day one
opts.zh: 是——每家公司從第一天起就有護城河趨勢

opts.en: No — the tool assumes a moat is already established enough to have a direction worth tracking; a company still proving product-market fit needs a different question first
opts.zh: 不是——這套工具假設護城河已經存在到值得追蹤方向的程度；一家還在驗證產品市場契合度的公司，該先問的是別的問題

opts.en: Yes, but only if the company is already profitable
opts.zh: 是，但前提是這家公司已經開始獲利

exp.en: This lesson names its own boundary condition explicitly: the framework works poorly for a company that has not yet established a durable advantage to track a direction on. The more useful question for an early-stage company is about product-market fit and unit economics, not widening or narrowing.
exp.zh: 這一課明確點出自己的邊界條件：對一家還沒建立起持久優勢、沒有方向可以追蹤的公司來說，這套框架用起來效果很差。對一家早期公司更有用的問題，是產品市場契合度和單位經濟，不是變寬還是變窄。

q.en: A packaged-food company shows stable gross margins for three straight years after a large merger — on the surface, a textbook sign of an intact brand moat. Underneath, its retail customers keep negotiating tighter wholesale terms every year, and the stable margin is being held up mostly by cost cuts rather than pricing power. Which kind of narrowing does this describe, and why does it matter?
q.zh: 一家包裝食品公司在一次大型併購後，連續 3 年毛利率都很穩定——表面上看是品牌護城河完好的教科書訊號。但底下，它的零售通路客戶每年都在談出更緊的批發條件，而毛利率的穩定主要是靠砍成本撐住，不是靠定價權。這描述的是哪一種變窄，為什麼這個區分重要？

opts.en: Internal, technology-driven narrowing — the same shape as a chipmaker falling behind on process nodes
opts.zh: 內部的、技術驅動的變窄——跟晶片廠製程落後是同一種型態

opts.en: External, value-chain narrowing — the pressure is coming from a customer's bargaining power, not from the company falling behind technologically, and a stable headline margin can hide it for years until a write-down forces it into the open
opts.zh: 外部的、價值鏈上的變窄——壓力來自客戶的議價能力，不是公司在技術上落後，而穩定的表面毛利率可以把這件事藏上好幾年，直到一次減損才把它逼到檯面上

opts.en: Neither — stable gross margins for three years is itself proof the moat is not narrowing at all
opts.zh: 都不是——連續 3 年毛利率穩定，本身就證明護城河根本沒有在變窄

exp.en: This lesson draws a distinction between narrowing that originates inside the company (falling behind on technology, the Intel shape) and narrowing that originates outside it (a counterparty in the value chain gaining bargaining power while the income statement looks calm). A stable blended gross margin can mask years of quiet concession-granting, because cost discipline and portfolio mix can offset pricing pressure right up until an impairment charge forces the accumulated damage onto one line of the income statement at once.
exp.zh: 這一課區分了兩種變窄：一種源自公司內部（技術上落後，英特爾那種型態），另一種源自公司外部（價值鏈上的對手方議價能力變強，但損益表看起來風平浪靜）。一個穩定的綜合毛利率，可以把好幾年默默讓步的過程藏起來，因為成本紀律和產品組合可以暫時抵銷定價壓力，一直到一次減損提列，才把累積的傷害一次逼進損益表的某一行。

q.en: A warehouse retailer that earns most of its operating profit from membership fees has reported a renewal rate climbing for seven straight years, and absorbed a fee increase two years ago with no dip. This year the rate slips from 92.7% to 92.3%. The company's annual report attributes the slip to a growing share of memberships sold online through promotions, which renew at a slightly lower rate. What is the most defensible way to record this reading?
q.zh: 一家主要靠會員費賺取營業利益的量販店，續會率已經連續 7 年往上，兩年前調漲會費也沒有讓它掉下來。今年這個數字從 92.7%退到 92.3%。公司年報把原因寫成：透過網路搭配促銷入會的比重變高，而這批會員的續會率平均低一點。這個讀數最站得住腳的記法是什麼？

opts.en: Log it as one reading that still needs its explanation tested — and write the test down: if the slide continues after the channel-mix effect has washed through, the widening call has lost its second supporting indicator
opts.zh: 把它記成一個「解釋還沒被驗證」的讀數，並且把驗證方式寫下來：如果通路組合的效果過去之後數字還在往下，變寬的判斷就失去了第二項支撐指標

opts.en: Flip the call to narrowing — a falling retention number is a falling retention number, whatever the explanation
opts.zh: 直接改判變窄——留存率下滑就是下滑，公司怎麼解釋都一樣

opts.en: Ignore it — management has already explained the cause, and 0.4 of a percentage point is inside the noise
opts.zh: 忽略它——公司已經解釋過原因了，而且 0.4 個百分點本來就在雜訊範圍內

exp.en: Both wrong answers skip a step. Flipping the call on a single 0.4-point move breaks the threshold rule this lesson sets out: one indicator moving once is noise, and a verdict needs at least two indicators moving over more than one quarter. But accepting the company's explanation and filing the reading away is the opposite failure — a management explanation is a claim, and this one happens to be checkable, because a channel-mix effect washes through within a few years while a genuine loss of appeal does not. Writing down what would have to happen for the explanation to fail is what keeps a trend call falsifiable instead of turning it into a story that absorbs every new number.
exp.zh: 兩個錯的選項都跳過了一個步驟。只憑一次 0.4 個百分點的變動就改判，違反這一課的門檻規則：一項指標動一次是雜訊，要下判定至少需要兩項指標、動超過一個季度。但接受公司的解釋、把這個讀數收進抽屜，則是反方向的失誤——公司的解釋是一個主張，而這個主張剛好可以驗證，因為通路組合造成的影響幾年內就會過去，真正的吸引力流失不會。把「這個解釋要在什麼情況下算失效」先寫下來，才能讓趨勢判斷保持可以被推翻，而不是變成一個能把任何新數字都吸收掉的故事。

q.en: A company reports total revenue growth of 18% for the year. Its earnings release discloses volume contributed 3 points, price contributed 2 points, and mix contributed 1 point. What is the acquisition contribution, and what does it imply?
q.zh: 一家公司公布今年總營收成長 18%。財報新聞稿揭露量貢獻了 3 個百分點、價貢獻了 2 個百分點、組合貢獻了 1 個百分點。併購貢獻是多少，這代表什麼？

opts.en: All 18 points are organic; acquisitions contributed nothing
opts.zh: 18 個百分點全部都是有機成長；併購沒有貢獻

opts.en: 6 points came from acquisitions, so the growth is mostly organic
opts.zh: 6 個百分點來自併購，所以這個成長大部分是有機的

opts.en: 12 points came from acquisitions — two-thirds of the headline growth came from buying revenue, not from the existing business
opts.zh: 12 個百分點來自併購——頭條成長裡有三分之二是買來的營收，不是既有業務長出來的

opts.en: This cannot be determined from the information given
opts.zh: 根據已知資訊無法判斷

exp.en: Organic contribution = volume + price + mix = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 points. Acquisition contribution = total 18 − organic 6 = 12 points. Twelve of eighteen points, two-thirds, came from buying revenue rather than growing the existing business — a growth pattern much closer to the Valeant shape than a headline 18% suggests on its own.
exp.zh: 有機貢獻 ＝ 量 ＋ 價 ＋ 組合 ＝ 3 ＋ 2 ＋ 1 ＝ 6 個百分點。併購貢獻 ＝ 總成長 18 − 有機 6 ＝ 12 個百分點。18 個百分點裡有 12 個、三分之二，來自買營收而不是既有業務自己長出來的——這個成長型態，比單看頭條 18% 更接近 Valeant 的樣子。

q.en: A product has reached an estimated 78% penetration in its core addressable market, and revenue growth has decelerated from 35% three years ago to 12% today. Management calls the slowdown “concerning.” What is the most likely correct read?
q.zh: 一項產品在核心可觸及市場的滲透率估計已達 78%，營收成長率從三年前的 35% 降到現在的 12%。經營層稱這是「令人擔憂的減速」。最可能正確的讀法是什麼？

opts.en: Definite proof the company is losing to competitors
opts.zh: 確鑿證明公司正在輸給競爭對手

opts.en: Mostly the natural arithmetic of running low on new customers near the top of the S-curve, not a sign of a competitive or execution failure
opts.zh: 大部分是靠近 S 曲線頂端、新客戶用光的自然算術結果，不是競爭力或執行力出問題的訊號

opts.en: Proof the original addressable-market estimate must have been wrong
opts.zh: 證明當初的可觸及市場估計一定是錯的

opts.en: Irrelevant — the company should simply spend more on marketing to reaccelerate to 35%
opts.zh: 無關緊要——公司只要加碼行銷支出，就應該能重新加速回到 35%

exp.en: At roughly 78% penetration, most of the addressable customers already own the product; deceleration at this stage is what the S-curve predicts by construction, not evidence of a weaker business. Treating every slowdown above the rough 70% marker as a red flag misreads arithmetic for a report card.
exp.zh: 滲透率大約來到 78% 時，大部分可觸及的客戶都已經是既有用戶；這個階段的減速，正是 S 曲線本來就會預測到的結果，不是生意變弱的證據。把超過大約 70% 界線之後的每一次減速都當成警訊，是把算術誤讀成了成績單。

q.en: Company X's investor day shows a new division folded into a vague “Other” segment with a $500B TAM slide, widening losses for six straight years, and no separately disclosed revenue. Company Y quietly starts disclosing a new segment this year showing $6B revenue with operating margin that has risen from break-even to 22% over the past four years. Which is closer to a real second curve?
q.zh: X 公司的法說日展示一個新事業，折疊在一個模糊的「其他」科目裡，配一張 5,000 億美元潛在市場的投影片，虧損已連續擴大六年，沒有獨立揭露營收。Y 公司今年才第一次悄悄揭露一個新分部，顯示營收 60 億美元，營業利益率過去四年從打平升到 22%。哪一家比較接近真正的第二曲線？

opts.en: Company X, because its addressable-market slide is bigger
opts.zh: X 公司，因為它的潛在市場投影片比較大

opts.en: Both equally, since both are receiving investment
opts.zh: 兩家一樣好，因為兩家都在投資這件事

opts.en: Neither, since second-curve stories are always overhyped
opts.zh: 兩家都不算，因為第二曲線的故事永遠都是誇大的

opts.en: Company Y — it clears all three checkable thresholds (disclosed revenue, multi-period improving unit economics, capital already committed), even though the market only started paying attention now
opts.zh: Y 公司——它三個可查證的門檻都到位了（已揭露營收、跨多期改善的單位經濟、已投入的資本），即使市場現在才開始注意到它

exp.en: A large TAM slide costs nothing to produce and Company X is missing all three thresholds. Company Y has independently disclosed revenue and a margin trend that has demonstrably improved for four straight years — exactly the AWS shape from the war story, where real progress sat inside a blended number for years before the market noticed.
exp.zh: 一張很大的潛在市場投影片，做出來幾乎不花成本，而 X 公司三個門檻一個都沒有。Y 公司有獨立揭露的營收，以及連續四年確實在改善的利潤率趨勢——正是戰爭故事裡 AWS 的型態：真實的進展在合併數字裡藏了好幾年，市場才注意到。

q.en: A company's ROIC is 7%, its estimated cost of capital is 11%, and it just announced it will nearly double capital expenditure to accelerate growth from 8% to 18% a year. What is the most likely effect on shareholder value?
q.zh: 一家公司 ROIC 是 7%，估計的資金成本是 11%，它剛宣布要把資本支出幾乎翻倍，把成長率從 8% 加速到 18%。這最可能對股東價值造成什麼影響？

opts.en: Value destruction will accelerate, because more capital is now being deployed at a return below its cost
opts.zh: 價值摧毀會加速，因為現在有更多資本被投在一個低於資金成本的報酬率上

opts.en: Value creation will accelerate, because growth is accelerating
opts.zh: 價值創造會加速，因為成長率正在加速

opts.en: There is no effect, since ROIC and growth rate are unrelated
opts.zh: 沒有影響，因為 ROIC 跟成長率無關

opts.en: Value creation, because higher capital spending signals management confidence
opts.zh: 價值創造，因為更高的資本支出代表經營層有信心

exp.en: With ROIC below WACC, every incremental dollar reinvested has a negative net present value the moment it is spent. Doubling capex to grow faster does not offset that gap — it deploys more capital at the losing rate, which destroys value faster, exactly the mechanism this lesson names explicitly.
exp.zh: 當 ROIC 低於 WACC，每多投入一塊錢，一花出去淨現值就是負的。把資本支出翻倍去換更快的成長，不會抵銷這個缺口——反而是把更多資本投在虧錢的報酬率上，摧毀價值的速度只會更快，這正是這一課明白點出的機制。

q.en: An analyst applies Rule of 40 (growth% + FCF margin%) to a mature, profitable regional bank growing revenue 3% a year with a 25% FCF margin (score 28, labeled “unhealthy”), and separately to a commodity chemicals producer whose FCF margin swings between −10% and +25% purely with the commodity price cycle. What is the most likely problem?
q.zh: 一位分析師把 Rule of 40（成長率% ＋ FCF 利潤率%）套用在一家成熟獲利的區域銀行上——營收年成長 3%、FCF 利潤率 25%（分數 28，標記「不健康」），也套用在一家 FCF 利潤率完全隨商品價格循環在 −10% 到 +25% 之間擺動的大宗化工廠上。最可能的問題是什麼？

opts.en: The bank's score of 28 correctly flags it as an unhealthy business
opts.zh: 銀行的分數 28 正確標記出它是一家不健康的公司

opts.en: Rule of 40 is being applied outside its intended range — it is built for unprofitable, thin-margin, deliberately growth-over-profit companies, not a mature profitable compounder or a cyclical business
opts.zh: Rule of 40 被套用在它原本不適用的範圍——它是為了未獲利、薄利、刻意選擇成長優先於獲利的公司設計的，不適合成熟獲利的複利公司或循環性生意

opts.en: Rule of 40 should always replace ROIC as the primary tool for every company
opts.zh: Rule of 40 應該永遠取代 ROIC，成為量所有公司的主要工具

opts.en: The chemicals producer's swinging FCF margin proves its accounting is fraudulent
opts.zh: 化工廠 FCF 利潤率忽高忽低，證明它的會計數字有造假

exp.en: Rule of 40 was built to keep from mistakenly punishing an early-stage, deliberately unprofitable company for burning cash to grow fast. A mature bank that is not trying to grow fast at all will fail the arithmetic simply by being what it is, and a commodity producer's margin swings with the cycle for reasons that have nothing to do with a growth-versus-profitability tradeoff — ROIC and incremental ROIC are the right tools for both.
exp.zh: Rule of 40 原本是為了不要誤判一家早期、刻意未獲利的公司——它燒錢是為了換快速成長。一家根本沒打算快速成長的成熟銀行，光是做自己該做的事就會過不了這條算式；大宗商品廠的利潤率隨循環擺動，跟成長對獲利的取捨完全無關——這兩者都該改用 ROIC 跟增量 ROIC 才是對的工具。

q.en: A small-cap company has posted revenue growth above 25% for eight consecutive years — well above the roughly single-digit-percentage share of public companies that sustain 20%-plus growth for a full decade. What is the appropriately skeptical next step, instead of simply celebrating the streak?
q.zh: 一家小型公司連續八年營收成長都超過 25%——遠高於能維持 10 年 20% 以上成長的公司，在所有上市公司裡通常只占個位數百分比的比例。比起單純為這個紀錄叫好，比較恰當、帶著懷疑的下一步是什麼？

opts.en: Specifically check how much of that growth has been funded by debt, share issuance, or acquisitions, since the base rate says most companies sustaining this pace this long are getting outside help
opts.zh: 具體去查這個成長有多少是靠舉債、發股或併購撐出來的——因為基準率說多數能撐這麼久、這麼快的公司，背後都有外部幫手

opts.en: Assume it is a rare generational compounder and stop checking further
opts.zh: 直接認定它是難得一見的世代複利股，不用再查了

opts.en: Assume the reported numbers must be fraudulent
opts.zh: 直接假設公布的數字一定造假

opts.en: Ignore the base rate, since every company is different
opts.zh: 不用管基準率，因為每家公司都不一樣

exp.en: A low base rate is not proof any specific company is faking it — it is a prompt to run exactly the tools this lesson built: the volume/price/mix/M&A decomposition, the incremental-ROIC-based internal growth ceiling, and the ROIC-versus-WACC spread, before deciding whether the streak is self-funded compounding or growth with help.
exp.zh: 低基準率不能拿來證明某一家公司在造假。它只是一個提醒：真的把這一課建立的工具跑一遍——量／價／組合／併購拆解、以增量 ROIC 算出的內生成長天花板、ROIC 對 WACC 的利差——再判斷這個紀錄究竟是自己造血複利出來的，還是靠外力撐出來的。

q.en: Two companies both show durable 15% organic growth, ROIC comfortably above WACC, and long penetration runway. Company A trades at 15× forward earnings; Company B trades at 45× forward earnings. What does this lesson's framework say about which is the better buy?
q.zh: 兩家公司都顯示出持久的 15% 有機成長、ROIC 明顯高於 WACC、滲透率跑道也還很長。A 公司交易在 15 倍預估本益比，B 公司交易在 45 倍預估本益比。這一課的框架，對於哪一家比較好買，說了什麼？

opts.en: Company A is automatically the better buy because it is cheaper
opts.zh: A 公司自動比較好買，因為比較便宜

opts.en: This lesson cannot answer that by itself — both pass as good businesses on the growth-quality tests here; whether the price already reflects that quality is a separate question this lesson does not cover
opts.zh: 這一課本身無法回答這個問題——兩家公司在這一課的成長品質測試上都算好生意；現在的價格有沒有已經反映這份品質，是這一課沒有處理的另一個問題

opts.en: Company B is automatically the better buy because a higher multiple confirms the market agrees it is a great business
opts.zh: B 公司自動比較好買，因為更高的本益比證明市場也同意它是一家好公司

opts.en: They are equally good buys, since growth quality is identical
opts.zh: 兩家一樣好買，因為成長品質完全一樣

exp.en: Everything built in this lesson answers whether the business itself is a good one — genuine, capital-efficient, value-creating growth. It says nothing about whether 15× or 45× already prices that quality in, which is deliberately left to the later lessons on market pricing and valuation.
exp.zh: 這一課建立的每一個工具，回答的都是「這門生意本身是不是好生意」——成長是不是真的、資本效率高不高、有沒有創造價值。它完全沒有回答 15 倍或 45 倍，有沒有已經把這份品質定價進去，這是刻意留給後面談市場定價與估值那幾課處理的問題。

q.en: A company's cash flow statement shows about $4.3B spent on acquisitions in a single year, in which total revenue grew about 11%. The company discloses every deal in its 10-K's business-combinations footnote and has compounded successfully this way for decades. What is the correct read?
q.zh: 一家公司的現金流量表顯示，單一一年花了大約 43 億美元在收購上，同一年總營收成長大約 11%。這家公司在 10-K 的併購附註裡揭露了每一筆交易，而且用這個方法穩健複利了好幾十年。正確的讀法是什麼？

opts.en: Heavy disclosed M&A spend by itself proves the growth is low quality
opts.zh: 光是揭露出來的高額併購支出，就足以證明這個成長品質很低

opts.en: Because total revenue grew, none of it needs to be checked against the acquisitions line
opts.zh: 因為總營收有成長，就不需要再去對照併購支出這一行

opts.en: Heavy M&A spend is not automatically a red flag — what matters is whether it is disclosed and part of a repeatable strategy versus hidden and undisclosed, which is exactly why the acquisitions line is the first thing worth checking before crediting a headline rate to the existing business
opts.zh: 高額併購支出不會自動變成警訊——重點在於它是不是被揭露、是不是一套可重複的策略，還是被藏起來、沒有揭露；這正是為什麼在把頭條成長率算給既有業務之前，併購支出這一行是第一個該查的地方

opts.en: The acquisitions line only matters for companies with negative free cash flow
opts.zh: 併購支出這一行，只對自由現金流是負的公司才有意義

exp.en: A large, fully disclosed acquisitions line does not by itself distinguish a struggling roll-up from a well-run serial acquirer — both can show the same cash flow statement line. What separates them is disclosure quality and whether the strategy has actually compounded value over time, which is exactly why checking the line is the first step, not the last word.
exp.zh: 一行龐大但完整揭露的併購支出，本身無法區分一台苦撐的併購拼裝車跟一家經營得很好的常勝併購者——兩者在現金流量表上可能長得一模一樣。真正能分辨兩者的，是揭露品質，以及這套策略長期下來是不是真的在複利價值；這正是為什麼查這一行只是第一步，不是最終結論。

q.en: A subscription business's total revenue growth decelerated from roughly 19% to roughly 6.5–6.7% as its most mature market approached full penetration, then reaccelerated to roughly 16% two years later — not because that same mature market found new households, but because the company launched a lower-priced tier aimed at a different kind of customer. What does the reacceleration illustrate?
q.zh: 一家訂閱制公司的總營收成長率，從大約 19% 減速到大約 6.5% 到 6.7%，同一時期它最成熟的市場滲透率已接近飽和；但兩年後成長率又回升到大約 16%，原因是公司推出了一個瞄準不同客群的低價方案，不是同一個成熟市場又冒出新家戶。這次回升說明了什麼？

opts.en: That the original deceleration reading was a mistake all along
opts.zh: 當初的減速讀法其實從一開始就是錯的

opts.en: That above roughly 70% penetration, further growth requires a genuinely new use case or customer segment, not more of the same product sold to the same pool of people
opts.zh: 滲透率超過大約 70% 之後，接下來的成長需要一個真正新的使用情境或客群，不能只是把同一個產品再賣給同一群人一次

opts.en: That penetration thresholds do not apply to subscription businesses
opts.zh: 滲透率門檻對訂閱制生意不適用

opts.en: That the company's organic growth figures cannot be trusted
opts.zh: 這證明這家公司公布的有機成長數字不可信

exp.en: The deceleration was the correct read at the time — it was the natural arithmetic of a maturing core market. The reacceleration did not overturn that read; it came from a genuinely new lever (a lower-priced tier reaching previously unpaying viewers), which is precisely the escape hatch this section names for a business running low on runway in its original market.
exp.zh: 當時的減速讀法本身沒有錯——那就是核心市場走向成熟的自然算術結果。後來的回升並沒有推翻那個讀法，而是來自一個真正新的槓桿（一個觸及原本不付費觀看者的低價方案），這正是本節替一個原本市場快沒有跑道的生意，點名的那個逃生門。

q.en: A company introduces a new "adjusted operating income" metric for the first time in the same quarter that GAAP operating income missed expectations, excluding a cost category that has also appeared as an exclusion in the two prior quarters. What should an analyst do?
q.zh: 一家公司在 GAAP 營業利益不如預期的同一季，第一次推出「調整後營業利益」這個新指標，排除的成本項目，前兩季也曾以排除項目的名義出現過。分析者該怎麼做？

opts.en: Use the adjusted figure since management presumably knows the business best
opts.zh: 採用調整後數字，因為管理層照理說最了解自己的生意

opts.en: Ignore the new metric entirely and only ever look at GAAP figures
opts.zh: 完全忽略這個新指標，永遠只看 GAAP 數字

opts.en: Report the company to regulators
opts.zh: 向監管機關檢舉這家公司

opts.en: Read exactly what is excluded, check whether the same exclusion category recurs quarter after quarter, and treat a recurring "one-time" cost as a real, ongoing cost of the business
opts.zh: 讀清楚排除了什麼，檢查同一類排除項目是不是季季重複出現，並把反覆出現的「一次性」成本，當成生意真正、持續存在的成本

exp.en: A brand-new adjusted metric arriving right after a weak GAAP quarter, excluding a cost that keeps recurring, is exactly the pattern this lesson's pitfall section describes. The fix is not to ignore all non-GAAP figures forever, but to check whether the exclusion is genuinely one-time or has become a recurring cost dressed up as an exception.
exp.zh: 一個全新的調整後指標，剛好在一個疲弱的 GAAP 季度之後出現，排除的又是一項反覆發生的成本，這正是這一課陷阱段落描述的模式。解方不是從此永遠忽略所有非 GAAP 數字，而是去檢查這項排除，到底是真的一次性，還是已經變成一項被包裝成例外的常態成本。

q.en: A company's net debt/EBITDA ratio looks comfortable at 1.8 times. Which additional piece of information would most change an assessment of its survivability in a downturn?
q.zh: 一家公司的淨負債／EBITDA 比率看起來很舒適，只有 1.8 倍。以下哪一項額外資訊，最可能改變對它在景氣下滑中存續力的評估？

opts.en: The company's stock price over the last year
opts.zh: 這家公司過去一年的股價走勢

opts.en: Whether 65% of that debt matures within the next 12 months and the credit facility carries a leverage covenant
opts.zh: 這些負債裡有沒有 65% 會在未來 12 個月內到期，以及信用額度是否附帶槓桿契約條款

opts.en: The number of analysts covering the stock
opts.zh: 覆蓋這檔股票的分析師人數

opts.en: The company's headquarters location
opts.zh: 這家公司總部的所在地

exp.en: The leverage ratio is an average that says nothing about timing or terms. A concentrated maturity wall combined with a covenant that can trigger a technical default is exactly the kind of detail that turns a comfortable-looking average into a real survivability risk.
exp.zh: 槓桿比率是一個平均值，完全沒告訴你時間點或條件。負債到期集中的到期牆，再加上一項可能觸發技術性違約的契約條款，正是那種能把一個看起來很舒適的平均值，變成真正存續力風險的細節。

q.en: Which of the following is the strongest single reason to treat a company's voluntary, self-harming accounting change — one that lowers this quarter's reported profit — as a positive signal about management honesty?
q.zh: 以下哪一項，是把一家公司自願、對自己不利的會計政策變動——一項會壓低本季申報利潤的變動——視為管理層誠信正面訊號的最強理由？

opts.en: A manager willing to report a worse number than the old policy would have produced has no obvious short-term incentive to do so unless the change reflects genuine economic reality
opts.zh: 一個願意呈報出比舊政策下更差數字的管理者，除非這項變動真的反映了經濟現實，否則沒有明顯的短期誘因去這麼做

opts.en: Management is legally required to make such changes
opts.zh: 管理層在法律上被要求要做這種變動

opts.en: Accounting changes are always disclosed in the same place
opts.zh: 會計政策變動一律揭露在同一個地方

opts.en: It guarantees the company will beat next quarter's estimates
opts.zh: 這保證了公司下一季一定會超越預期

exp.en: The logic is about incentives: most accounting choices that get made voluntarily tilt toward flattering the current number, so a voluntary choice that does the opposite is one of the few signals not distorted by that incentive. It is one useful data point, not a guarantee about anything else in the filing.
exp.zh: 這個邏輯是關於誘因：大多數自願做出的會計選擇，都會傾向讓當下的數字好看，所以一個反其道而行的自願選擇，是少數不會被那個誘因扭曲的訊號之一。它是一個有用的資料點，不是對財報裡其他任何事情的保證。

q.en: A software company shows operating cash flow consistently exceeding net income by a wide margin every quarter. Which explanation is most plausible for a subscription business?
q.zh: 一家軟體公司，每一季的營業現金流都持續大幅超過淨利。對一家訂閱制生意來說，哪個解釋最合理？

opts.en: It must be manipulating its cash flow statement
opts.zh: 它一定在操縱現金流量表

opts.en: The company has no depreciation expense
opts.zh: 這家公司沒有折舊費用

opts.en: Customers commonly prepay annual subscriptions in cash while the revenue is recognized ratably over the year, so deferred revenue growth boosts cash ahead of reported earnings
opts.zh: 客戶通常是預先用現金付清整年訂閱費，而營收卻是按月分攤認列，所以遞延收入的成長會讓現金領先申報利潤入帳

opts.en: This pattern is impossible under standard accounting rules
opts.zh: 這種模式在一般會計準則下是不可能發生的

exp.en: Cash exceeding net income is not automatically suspicious — the direction matters as much as the divergence. A subscription business collecting cash upfront and recognizing revenue over time is a textbook honest reason for cash to run ahead of reported profit, the mirror image of the accrual-heavy warning pattern.
exp.zh: 現金超過淨利，本身並不自動可疑——方向跟落差本身一樣重要。一家訂閱制生意先收現金、再隨時間認列營收，是現金領先申報利潤一個教科書等級的誠實理由，正好跟應計偏高的警訊模式互為鏡像。

q.en: A company you are analyzing turns out to be a regional commercial bank, and its cash flow statement shows what looks like a deeply negative free cash flow every year. What is the correct read?
q.zh: 你正在分析的一家公司，結果是一家區域商業銀行，它的現金流量表每年都顯示出看似極度為負的自由現金流。正確的解讀是什麼？

opts.en: This is a severe red flag identical to the warning signs described earlier in this lesson
opts.zh: 這是跟這一課前面描述的警訊完全一樣的嚴重紅旗

opts.en: This lesson's standard free-cash-flow framework does not transfer cleanly to a bank, because loan growth is recorded as a cash outflow even in a healthy year
opts.zh: 這一課的標準自由現金流架構，沒辦法直接套用到銀行身上，因為就算是健康的一年，放款成長也會被記成現金流出

opts.en: The bank is definitely insolvent
opts.zh: 這家銀行一定已經資不抵債

opts.en: Banks are not required to file cash flow statements
opts.zh: 銀行不需要申報現金流量表

exp.en: This is the explicit boundary condition raised earlier: banks fund lending with deposits, and a growing loan book shows up as a cash outflow in a healthy bank, not a distress signal. Applying a standard operating-company checklist to a bank without adjustment produces a confidently wrong conclusion.
exp.zh: 這正是前面明確提到的邊界條件：銀行用存款支應放款，一本健康成長的放款簿，在現金流量表上就是會顯示成現金流出，這不是一個困境訊號。把一般營運型公司的檢查表，不做調整就套到銀行身上，得到的會是一個自信滿滿卻錯誤的結論。

q.en: An analyst confirms that a company reports honest, high-quality earnings with real cash backing and a manageable debt maturity schedule. What can be concluded about the stock?
q.zh: 一位分析者確認了一家公司申報的是誠實、高品質的利潤，有真實現金支撐，債務到期排程也可控。這對這檔股票能得出什麼結論？

opts.en: The stock is automatically a good investment at any price
opts.zh: 不管什麼價格，這檔股票自動就是一筆好投資

opts.en: The stock will outperform the market next quarter
opts.zh: 這檔股票下一季會跑贏大盤

opts.en: The company will never need to raise additional financing
opts.zh: 這家公司永遠不需要再融資

opts.en: Nothing about the stock yet — earnings quality describes the business, and whether the stock is attractive depends on what the current price already assumes about that business
opts.zh: 關於這檔股票還什麼都不能下結論——獲利品質描述的是這家公司本身，股票吸不吸引人，取決於目前的價格已經對這家公司假設了什麼

exp.en: Earnings quality is a statement about the business, not the stock. A high-quality business can still be a poor investment if the price already assumes flawless execution forever, and read-through thinking exists precisely to separate the two questions.
exp.zh: 獲利品質是關於這家公司本身的陳述，不是關於股票的陳述。就算是一門高品質的生意，如果價格早就已經假設它永遠完美執行，依然可能是一筆糟糕的投資，而讀透式思考存在的目的，正是把這兩個問題分開來看。

q.en: In an earlier lesson, a supply-side judgment concluded that a market was moving toward oligopoly with rational capacity discipline among the remaining players. A company in that market now reports revenue growing 25% while gross margin quietly compresses for three straight quarters. What is the most useful next step?
q.zh: 在較早一課裡，一項供給面的判斷認為，某個市場正在朝寡占發展，剩下的玩家也維持理性的產能紀律。這個市場裡的一家公司，現在申報營收成長 25%，但毛利率卻連續三季悄悄壓縮。最有用的下一步是什麼？

opts.en: Assume the supply-side judgment was wrong and the market has become irrationally competitive
opts.zh: 假設之前的供給面判斷是錯的，這個市場已經變得非理性競爭

opts.en: Treat the margin compression as a specific test of the prior oligopoly judgment — check whether it comes from price competition among the disciplined players, or from a genuinely lower-margin product mix, before concluding either way
opts.zh: 把毛利率壓縮，當成對先前寡占判斷的一項具體測試——在下任何一個方向的結論之前，先查清楚它是來自紀律玩家之間的價格競爭，還是來自真的毛利較低的產品組合改變

opts.en: Ignore the margin trend since revenue growth is strong
opts.zh: 因為營收成長強勁，就忽略毛利率的走勢

opts.en: Conclude the company is manipulating its accounts
opts.zh: 斷定這家公司在操縱帳目

exp.en: This is read-through thinking applied across lessons: a prior structural judgment about the supply side generates a specific, falsifiable expectation about margins, and a new filing should be read as a test of that expectation rather than as an isolated number to explain away.
exp.zh: 這正是跨課應用的讀透式思考：一項先前關於供給面結構的判斷，會產生一個具體、可證偽的毛利率預期，而一份新財報，應該被當成對這個預期的一次測試來讀，而不是一個被單獨解釋掉的孤立數字。

q.en: A company's disclosed insurance-liability reserves for a legacy business line have grown for three straight years as old assumptions are updated toward reality. Separately, a well-known forensic short seller publishes a report alleging the reserves are still understated by tens of billions of dollars, and the stock falls sharply the next day before mostly recovering over the following months with no regulatory action. What is the most balanced read of this pair of facts?
q.zh: 一家公司針對一項舊業務線揭露的保險負債準備金，已經連續三年成長，因為舊的假設正被更新、貼近現實。另外，一位知名鑑識派放空機構發表報告，指控準備金仍被低估數百億美元，股價隔天大跌，之後幾個月大致回升，且監管機關沒有採取行動。對這兩件事最平衡的解讀是什麼？

opts.en: The multi-year reserve growth is itself a real, disclosed signal worth tracking, but a single dramatic allegation is not automatic proof — the two need to be checked against each other rather than either one taken at face value
opts.zh: 連年成長的準備金本身，是一個真實、有揭露的訊號，值得追蹤；但單一則聲勢浩大的指控，不自動等於證據——這兩者需要互相對照查證，不能只取其中一個當真

opts.en: Since the stock mostly recovered and no regulator acted, the allegation was entirely baseless and the reserve trend can be ignored
opts.zh: 既然股價大致回升、監管機關也沒動作，代表這則指控完全沒有根據，準備金的趨勢可以忽略

opts.en: Since the reserves kept growing for three years, the short seller must have been right and the recovery was the market being slow to react
opts.zh: 既然準備金連三年成長，代表放空機構一定是對的，股價回升只是市場反應太慢

opts.en: Neither fact is relevant to earnings quality since insurance reserves are actuarial estimates, not cash items
opts.zh: 這兩件事都跟獲利品質無關，因為保險準備金是精算估計，不是現金項目

exp.en: This mirrors the GE/Markopolos episode described in this lesson: a multi-year, disclosed reserve build is a genuine signal worth tracking on its own terms, while a single loud allegation — however credentialed the source — is a separate claim that has to be checked against the filings rather than assumed to be either confirmed or refuted by the stock's short-term price reaction.
exp.zh: 這正對應這一課提到的 GE／Markopolos 事件：連續多年、有揭露的準備金增提，本身就是值得追蹤的真實訊號；而一則聲量很大的指控，不管出處多有資歷，是另一件需要拿去跟財報對照查證的主張，不能單靠股價的短期反應，就假設它被證實或被推翻。

q.en: A company with 30% ROIC, far above its cost of capital, spends almost all its free cash flow every year acquiring businesses in unrelated industries at large premiums, with a weak record of integration. Revenue grows but ROIC on the combined entity keeps drifting down. What is most likely happening?
q.zh: 一家公司 ROIC 高達 30%，遠高於資金成本，卻幾乎每年都把所有自由現金流拿去併購不相關產業的公司，而且付出很高的溢價，整合紀錄也不好。營收持續成長，但合併後整體 ROIC 卻一直往下滑。這最可能是什麼情況？

opts.en: The company is smartly diversifying away from a saturated core market
opts.zh: 公司正在聰明地分散風險，跳出已經飽和的本業

opts.en: A high starting ROIC guarantees any acquisition will still be a good use of capital
opts.zh: 起始 ROIC 夠高，代表任何併購都還是資本的好用途

opts.en: Empire building — capital is being deployed for size rather than for return, and the declining combined ROIC is the direct evidence
opts.zh: 帝國建造——資本被用來換取規模而不是報酬率，持續下滑的合併 ROIC 就是直接證據

opts.en: Revenue growth proves the strategy is working regardless of ROIC
opts.zh: 營收有成長就證明這套策略有效，跟 ROIC 無關

exp.en: A high standalone ROIC says nothing about whether new acquisitions bought at large premiums can earn a similar return, and the declining combined ROIC is direct evidence that capital is being spent on size rather than on return. Revenue growth is the weakest of the four pieces of evidence here precisely because acquisitions buy revenue mechanically.
exp.zh: 高的本業 ROIC 並不能保證用高溢價買來的新併購也能賺到類似報酬率，而持續下滑的合併 ROIC 正是資本被用來換規模、不是換報酬率的直接證據。營收成長在這四項證據裡反而最沒有份量，因為併購本來就會機械式地把營收買進來。

q.en: Company X buys back stock when its P/E is below its five-year median and below the peer median. Company Y buys back heavily when its P/E is at an all-time high, funded partly by new debt. Which is more likely creating shareholder value through its buybacks?
q.zh: 甲公司在本益比低於五年中位數、也低於同業中位數時回購股票。乙公司在本益比創歷史新高時大舉回購，部分資金還來自新借的債。哪一家透過回購創造股東價值的可能性比較大？

opts.en: Company Y, because buying more shows more conviction
opts.zh: 乙公司，因為買得更多代表更有信心

opts.en: Both are equally good, since both reduce the share count
opts.zh: 兩家都一樣好，因為都讓流通股數減少了

opts.en: Neither — buybacks never create shareholder value
opts.zh: 兩家都不算，因為回購本來就不會創造股東價值

opts.en: Company X, because it is buying below a reasonable value benchmark rather than at a cycle high
opts.zh: 甲公司，因為它是在低於合理估值基準時買進，不是在景氣循環高點買

exp.en: The direction of the wealth transfer in a buyback depends on the price paid, not on the dollar amount spent or the resulting drop in share count. X buying cheap transfers value to the shareholders who stay; Y buying expensive, with borrowed money, transfers it the other way. The tempting wrong answer is that both are equally good because the share count falls in both cases — the share count is the mechanism, not the outcome.
exp.zh: 回購的財富移轉方向，取決於買進的價格，不是花了多少錢或股數減少了多少。甲公司買便宜，把價值移轉給留下來的股東；乙公司買貴、還用借來的錢買，方向正好相反。最誘人的錯誤答案是「兩家一樣好，因為股數都變少了」——股數減少只是機制，不是結果。

q.en: A quarterly report's Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities table shows the company bought 1.0 million shares in month one at an average of $40, 1.0 million in month two at $52, and 4.0 million in month three at $61, the quarter's record high. What does this table let you see that the annual buyback total alone would not?
q.zh: 一份季報的「發行人買回權益證券」表顯示：公司第一個月用平均 40 美元買了 100 萬股，第二個月用 52 美元買了 100 萬股，第三個月用 61 美元買了 400 萬股，而 61 美元是這一季的最高價。這張表讓你看到什麼，是「全年回購總金額」這一個數字看不到的？

opts.en: Nothing new — the table only repeats the repurchase total already shown in the cash-flow statement
opts.zh: 看不到新東西——這張表只是重複現金流量表已經揭露的回購總額

opts.en: That two-thirds of the shares were bought in the single month the stock was most expensive, so the average price paid sits far above the quarter's low — the timing pattern, not just the amount
opts.zh: 三分之二的股數是在股價最貴的那一個月買進的，所以平均買進成本遠高於這一季的低點——看到的是買進的時點分布，不只是金額

opts.en: That the buyback was accretive to earnings per share
opts.zh: 看到這次回購讓每股盈餘增厚了

opts.en: That management believed the stock was undervalued at $61
opts.zh: 看到經營層認為股價在 61 美元時仍然被低估

exp.en: The monthly breakdown is the whole point of the table: an annual total of 6 million shares hides the fact that the money was concentrated at the top of the range. Average price paid, compared with the quarter's trading range, is the cheapest available read on whether repurchases were price-disciplined or calendar-driven.
exp.zh: 這張表的價值就在月度拆分：一個「全年買回 600 萬股」的總數，會蓋掉「錢集中花在區間頂部」這件事。把平均買進價格拿去跟這一季的交易區間比，是最省力的一種檢查——看回購到底是照價格做的，還是照行事曆做的。

q.en: Which of the following is the strongest positive signal of management honesty?
q.zh: 以下哪一項是經營層誠信最強的正面訊號？

opts.en: Management beats its own guidance by a wide margin nearly every single quarter
opts.zh: 經營層幾乎每一季都用很大的差距超越自己的財測

opts.en: Every annual shareholder letter for the past decade describes uninterrupted success with no mistakes
opts.zh: 過去十年的每一封股東信，內容都是沒有中斷過的成功故事、完全沒提到任何失誤

opts.en: Management maintains dividend growth every year no matter what happens to free cash flow
opts.zh: 不管自由現金流發生什麼事，經營層每年都維持股利成長

opts.en: Management voluntarily makes an accounting change that lowers this year's reported earnings, with no external requirement forcing it
opts.zh: 經營層在沒有任何外部要求的情況下，主動做出一項會讓本年度報告獲利變差的會計變更

exp.en: A self-harming disclosure costs management something real this year and buys nothing except more accurate future numbers, which is hard to fake. Chronic wide guidance beats usually indicate deliberately low guidance rather than honesty; a mistake-free multi-year record is itself a red flag, since no real business runs that cleanly; and a dividend defended regardless of free cash flow is the pattern this lesson flags as a warning, not as discipline.
exp.zh: 一項讓自己數字變差的揭露，本年度就要付出真實代價，換到的除了未來數字更準確之外什麼都沒有，這種訊號很難假裝。長期大幅超越財測，通常代表財測被刻意壓低，不代表誠實；連續多年完全沒有失誤的紀錄，本身就是警訊，因為沒有一家真實的公司能經營得這麼乾淨；而不管自由現金流如何都硬撐的股利，正是這一課點名的警訊，不是紀律。

q.en: A company has raised its dividend every year for 15 straight years. For the last 3 years, free cash flow has not covered the dividend, and net debt has been rising to fund the gap. How should the 15-year streak be read?
q.zh: 一家公司連續 15 年每年調升股利。但過去 3 年，自由現金流已經蓋不住配息，淨負債持續上升來補這個缺口。這個連續 15 年的紀錄該怎麼解讀？

opts.en: As a red flag — protecting the streak may itself have become the objective, funded by debt rather than by cash the business generates
opts.zh: 這是警訊——維持這個紀錄本身可能已經變成目標，靠負債而不是本業產出的現金撐著

opts.en: As strong reassurance — a streak this long essentially guarantees the dividend is safe
opts.zh: 這是強力的安心訊號——這麼長的連續紀錄，基本上保證了股利很安全

opts.en: As irrelevant — dividend policy says nothing about capital-allocation quality
opts.zh: 這無關緊要——股利政策跟資本配置品質沒有關係

opts.en: As proof management is disciplined, since they are willing to borrow rather than cut
opts.zh: 這證明經營層有紀律，因為他們寧可借錢也不願意砍股利

exp.en: A long streak sounds like discipline, but the actual test is free-cash-flow coverage checked every single year, not the length of the record. Once debt has to fund the gap, the streak has stopped being a byproduct of a healthy business and become a target defended for its own sake — which is precisely when a cut, arriving from a weaker balance sheet, does the most damage.
exp.zh: 連續紀錄聽起來像紀律，但真正的檢驗是每一年的自由現金流覆蓋率，不是紀錄有多長。一旦要靠負債補缺口，這個連續紀錄就不再是健康本業的自然結果，而變成一個為了自己而被硬守的目標——而那正是最後真的減發時，資產負債表也已經變弱、傷害最大的時刻。

q.en: Two CEOs are up for comparison. CEO A's bonus is weighted 80% toward EPS-growth targets. CEO B's bonus is weighted 80% toward ROIC and per-share value growth. In a year with excess cash but few good reinvestment opportunities, which CEO is structurally more likely to overpay for a large acquisition just to hit the target?
q.zh: 比較兩位執行長。甲執行長的獎金有 80% 綁在 EPS 成長目標上。乙執行長的獎金有 80% 綁在 ROIC 與每股價值成長上。在一個現金過剩、但找不到多少好的再投資機會的年份，哪位執行長在結構上更可能為了達成目標而買貴一筆大型併購？

opts.en: CEO B, because ROIC targets pressure management to grow the company by any means available
opts.zh: 乙執行長，因為 ROIC 目標會逼經營層不計代價地把公司做大

opts.en: CEO A, because an EPS-accretive deal satisfies that bonus formula almost regardless of the price paid
opts.zh: 甲執行長，因為一筆讓 EPS 增厚的交易，幾乎不管價格多貴，都能滿足他的獎金公式

opts.en: Neither — bonus structure has no measurable effect on acquisition behaviour
opts.zh: 兩位都不會——獎金結構對併購行為沒有可觀察的影響

opts.en: Both equally, since every executive faces the same pressure to grow
opts.zh: 兩位風險一樣，因為所有高管都面臨同樣的成長壓力

exp.en: An EPS-weighted bonus can be satisfied by an overpriced, debt-financed deal, because such deals are almost mechanically accretive. An ROIC-weighted bonus moves the other way: deploying capital at a poor return lowers the metric, so overpaying costs the executive personally. The distractor about ROIC forcing growth inverts the mechanism — a ratio with capital in the denominator punishes growth bought badly.
exp.zh: 重壓 EPS 的獎金，可以被一筆買貴、靠借債支應的交易滿足，因為這種交易幾乎在機械上就會增厚 EPS。重壓 ROIC 的獎金方向相反：把資本投到報酬率差的地方會讓指標下降，所以買貴這件事會直接讓高管自己付出代價。「ROIC 目標會逼人做大」這個干擾選項把機制顛倒了——分母是資本的比率，本來就會懲罰買得不划算的成長。

q.en: For which type of company would this lesson's five-year capital-allocation scorecard be the LEAST reliable to apply as described?
q.zh: 用這一課教的五年資本配置記分卡去分析下列哪一種公司，最不可靠？

opts.en: A mature industrial company with ten years of positive free cash flow and public filings
opts.zh: 一家成熟的工業公司，有十年正向自由現金流和公開財報紀錄

opts.en: A consumer staples company with a long dividend history
opts.zh: 一家有長期股利歷史的民生消費品公司

opts.en: A pre-profit, high-growth company still burning cash, with no meaningful free cash flow to allocate yet
opts.zh: 一家還沒獲利、正在燒錢的高成長公司，還沒有有意義的自由現金流可以分配

opts.en: A profitable industrial distributor with five years of acquisition history
opts.zh: 一家獲利中的工業經銷商，有五年併購紀錄

exp.en: The scorecard assumes meaningful positive free cash flow to rank across five options. A cash-burning company has nothing to allocate yet, so the relevant discipline at that stage is runway and burn rate rather than an allocation scorecard. A regulated bank or insurer is the other boundary case, since a regulator, not management judgment alone, sets how much capital can be returned.
exp.zh: 這套記分卡假設公司有有意義的正向自由現金流可以在五個選項間排序。一家還在燒錢的公司根本還沒有東西可以分配，這個階段真正該檢查的是現金跑道與燒錢速度，而不是配置記分卡。另一個邊界情況是受監管的銀行或保險公司，因為能還多少資本給股東是由監管機關決定，不只是經營層的判斷。

q.en: Three years ago a company acquired a competitor and promised about $400 million of annual run-rate cost synergies by year three. Two years after closing it folded the acquired unit into a larger reporting segment and stopped disclosing its results separately. Combined operating margin today is roughly where it was before the deal, and no goodwill has been written down. What is the most reasonable read?
q.zh: 三年前，一家公司併購了一個競爭對手，並承諾第三年達成每年約 4 億美元的成本綜效。交易完成兩年後，它把這個被併購的事業併進一個更大的報導分部，不再單獨揭露其成績。今天合併後的營業利益率大致還在交易前的水準，商譽也沒有認列過任何減損。最合理的解讀是什麼？

opts.en: The promised synergy most likely did not arrive — the margin line shows no trace of it, and the disclosure change removed the only way an outsider could ever verify the promise
opts.zh: 承諾的綜效很可能沒有出現——利益率上看不到任何痕跡，而揭露方式的改變，剛好拿掉了外部人唯一能驗證這個承諾的途徑

opts.en: Synergies routinely take longer than three years; the right response is to wait for the fourth-year numbers
opts.zh: 綜效本來就常常要超過三年才會出現，正確的做法是再等第四年的數字

opts.en: Merging reporting segments is a routine simplification and carries no information about the deal
opts.zh: 合併報導分部只是例行的簡化作業，跟這筆交易的成敗無關

opts.en: The absence of any goodwill impairment shows the deal worked as planned
opts.zh: 沒有認列任何商譽減損，代表這筆交易照計畫成功了

exp.en: Two of the three checks fail at once: the promised amount never showed up in the margin line by management's own deadline, and the segment disclosure that would have allowed verification disappeared before the deadline arrived. The absence of an impairment is the weakest possible evidence in the other direction — a large, never-impaired goodwill balance sitting next to an acquired business whose results are no longer visible is itself a quiet warning, not a clean bill of health.
exp.zh: 三項檢查裡有兩項同時不過關：承諾的金額在經營層自己設定的期限內從來沒有出現在利益率上，而能讓外部人驗證的分部揭露，又剛好在期限到達之前消失了。「沒有認列減損」則是反方向最沒力的證據——一筆龐大、從未減損過的商譽，旁邊是一個成績已經看不到的被併購事業，這本身就是安靜的警訊，不是健康證明。

q.en: A regional bank's free cash flow, computed with the standard formula, comes out to roughly negative $90 billion in a year when customer deposits grew rapidly. What should you conclude?
q.zh: 一家區域銀行用標準公式算出的自由現金流，在一個客戶存款快速成長的年度約為負 900 億美元。你該怎麼判讀？

opts.en: This is normal balance-sheet-driven behavior for the financial archetype, not cash burn
opts.zh: 這是金融原型正常的資產負債表驅動現象，不是燒錢

opts.en: The bank is almost certainly burning cash and heading toward trouble
opts.zh: 這家銀行幾乎肯定在燒錢，正走向麻煩

opts.en: This pattern is close to definitive proof of accounting fraud
opts.zh: 這個模式幾乎可以確定是做假帳的證據

opts.en: You should apply the compounder's FCF/NI cash-conversion threshold to decide
opts.zh: 你應該套用複利股的 FCF／淨利現金轉換門檻來判斷

exp.en: Deposits are a funding source; when they surge, the standard FCF formula reads the resulting loan and securities growth as a huge outflow, even though nothing is actually being burned. This is the mechanism at the center of this lesson, and it applies to the financial archetype specifically — not as a general excuse for any company with negative FCF.
exp.zh: 存款是一種資金來源；當存款大幅湧入，標準 FCF 公式會把隨之而來的放款與證券部位成長讀成一筆巨大流出，儘管實際上什麼都沒被燒掉。這正是這一課核心的機制，而且只適用於金融原型——不是任何負 FCF 公司都能套用的萬用藉口。

q.en: A SaaS company reports trailing EPS of -$1.20, revenue growth of 30% year over year, and a free cash flow margin of +12%. Which is the right way to judge it?
q.zh: 一家 SaaS 公司過去 12 個月每股盈餘為負 1.20 美元，營收年增 30%，自由現金流利潤率為正 12%。該怎麼判斷它？

opts.en: Compute PEG, since growth companies are always judged on PEG
opts.zh: 算 PEG，因為成長股一律用 PEG 判斷

opts.en: Debt-to-equity alone, since growth companies are judged purely on leverage
opts.zh: 只看負債權益比，因為成長股純粹用槓桿判斷

opts.en: Trailing P/E, since a low P/E always signals a bargain
opts.zh: 看過去本益比，因為低本益比一律代表便宜

opts.en: Rule of 40 (30 + 12 = 42) and net revenue retention — PEG is undefined and uninformative here
opts.zh: 算 40 法則（30+12=42）與淨營收留存率——PEG 在這裡無法定義也沒有資訊價值

exp.en: With negative trailing EPS, PEG is mathematically undefined — dividing a growth rate by a negative number produces nonsense, not a bearish signal. The Rule of 40 result of 42 is comfortably above the roughly-40 health threshold for this archetype.
exp.zh: 過去每股盈餘為負時，PEG 在數學上根本無法定義——用一個成長率去除以一個負數，得到的是無意義的結果，不是看空訊號。40 法則算出來的 42 明顯高於這種原型約 40 的健康門檻。

q.en: An industrial group reports consolidated ROIC of 11% and trades at 14x earnings, roughly in line with industrial peers. Its segment footnote shows that a wholly owned finance arm generated 45% of group operating profit last year. What does the archetype framework say to do?
q.zh: 一家工業集團合併 ROIC 為 11%，本益比 14 倍，大致與工業同業一致。它的部門附註顯示，一個百分之百持股的金融子公司去年貢獻了集團 45% 的營業利益。原型框架會怎麼處理？

opts.en: Nothing — consolidated ROIC and a peer-level multiple already capture the whole company
opts.zh: 不用處理——合併 ROIC 加上同業水準的倍數，已經完整描述了這家公司

opts.en: Split it: route the finance arm to the financial archetype and judge it on ROTCE and tangible book separately, because an industrial multiple applied to finance earnings prices a balance-sheet risk nobody has measured
opts.zh: 拆開來看：把金融子公司歸進金融原型，用 ROTCE 與有形帳面淨值單獨判斷，因為用工業股的倍數去乘金融業的盈餘，等於替一個沒有人量過的資產負債表風險定了價

opts.en: Discard the finance segment's profit entirely and value only the industrial segments
opts.zh: 直接把金融部門的獲利整個剔除，只替工業部門估值

opts.en: Apply the unprofitable-high-growth ruler, since mixed groups are hard to classify
opts.zh: 改用未獲利高成長的尺，因為混合型集團很難分類

exp.en: Two archetypes inside one set of statements is a category error one level up.
